title: Shrink sliding window size (long//4 instead of long//2)
description: Changed short_window = long_window // 2 to long_window // 4 in _compute_window_sizes (sequence_len//4 = 512 tokens instead of 1024), keeping WINDOW_PATTERN=SSSS and DEPTH=9 unchanged.
reflection: Clear win: val_bpb 0.993010 vs 0.998440 baseline, a -0.00543 improvement — over 10x larger than the SSSS win that established the baseline this round, and well outside the noise band we've seen elsewhere (~0.00005-0.0003). Confirms the hypothesized mechanism (less attention compute per step -> more steps/tokens in fixed 5-min budget) generalizes from window *frequency* (SSSL->SSSS) to window *size* (half->quarter context). Natural follow-up for whoever runs next round: bracket further, e.g. long_window//8, to see if the trend continues or reverses — quarter-context may not be the floor. Also worth someone re-checking DEPTH under this new (even cheaper) attention cost, since the compute-optimal depth argument from a0/a2's proposals applies here too, just doubly so.
